messages:
eva: Quick summary of the streaming vs non-streaming throughput/latency sweep across GPU families and regions. charts + raw CSV here: https://s3.redwood-internal/bench/1732109876/overview.png and https://s3.redwood-internal/bench/1732109876/data.csv :eyes:

Key high-level takeaways:
- Streaming (SSE/ws) gives ~2-3x lower p50 on tail-sensitive workloads but reduces peak RPS per GPU because of long-lived connections and KV-cache memory pressure. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
- Non-streaming (HTTP/short RPC) achieves higher absolute throughput (rps) with batching but has worse steady-state tail (p95) for interactive flows.
- H100 outperforms A100 on p50 for streaming when using fused attention + cuBLAS kernels; A100 still wins cost/throughput for large-batch non-streaming in us-west1.

mike: can we get a concise table with numbers? p50/p95 + rps per GPU for both modes and regions?

eva: pasted the trimmed numbers below (short threads):
```
Model: redwood-small-7B (fp16)
Test: 256 prompt tokens -> 128 completion tokens
Mode: streaming (SSE) / non-streaming (HTTP)
GPUs: A100-80GB, H100-80GB
Regions: us-west1, eu-west4, asia-southeast1

--- us-west1 / A100 ---
Streaming SSE: p50=78ms, p95=160ms, concurrent_streams_per_gpu=120, sustained_rps_equiv=85
Non-streaming: p50=120ms, p95=320ms, max_rps_per_gpu=280 (with batch_size=8)

--- us-west1 / H100 ---
Streaming SSE: p50=62ms, p95=140ms, concurrent_streams_per_gpu=140, sustained_rps_equiv=100
Non-streaming: p50=110ms, p95=260ms, max_rps_per_gpu=330 (batch_size=8)

--- eu-west4 (A100/H100 similar to us-west1 but +10-15% p95 penalty) ---
--- asia-southeast1 (higher p95 due to infra/peering) ---
```

arjun: kernel notes - on H100 we tested two kernel stacks: 1) fused-attn + cuBLAS matmul 2) triton-fused kernels. fused-attn + cuBLAS gave best single-request latency on streaming (lower p50), but triton gave better packing for batch throughput in non-streaming. memory copies during KV cache growth are the real limiter for streaming throughput; softpin and increased slab sizes help.

laura: region ops note: asia-southeast1 runs on older switch firmware in our test cluster, adds ~30-60ms variability at p95. should we mark asia as "experimental" for strict SLO?

mike: for capacity planning — what's a safe conservative QPS/gpu number to use in the console autoscaler for each mode?

eva: recommended conservative numbers (for redwood-small-7B, 99% payloads <= 512 tokens):
- Streaming: set target_concurrent_streams_per_gpu = 80 for A100, 100 for H100 (this keeps p95 under 200ms in worst-case region)
- Non-streaming: set target_rps_per_gpu = 200 for A100, 260 for H100 (batch_size tuned to 8; increase batch for higher throughput)

bench-bot: CSV uploaded -> https://s3.redwood-internal/bench/1732109876/data.csv ; auto-summary: streaming lowers p50 by 20-30% vs non-streaming; non-streaming increases peak rps by ~2.8x.

mike: nice. what's the quantization sensitivity? did INT8 change the tradeoffs?

eva: quick note: INT8 (per-tensor PG-Q) reduced memory pressure and increased rps by ~15% for non-streaming, but introduced occasional small regression in token-level quality on long-tail prompts (we flagged those in the eval suite). For streaming the memory wins are bigger (more concurrent streams fit), pushing concurrent_streams up ~10-15% on A100.

arjun: one more micro note: websocket fanout increases kernel cache churn if clients attach/detach fast. prefer SSE for simpler fanout semantics in our runtime unless you need bi-directional.

laura: action items:
- [eva] publish trimmed graphs and recommended autoscaler defaults to Console docs (ETA EOD Fri)
- [arjun] run softpin+slab-size sweep on H100 for streaming in eu-west4 (next 48h)
- [mike] update cost model with H100 streaming p95 numbers for sales deck

eva: ack. attaching perf command for reproducibility:
```
./rbench --model redwood-small-7B --mode streaming --duration 120 --concurrency 120 --gpu A100 --region us-west1 --tokens 384
./rbench --model redwood-small-7B --mode http --duration 120 --rps 300 --batch_size 8 --gpu A100 --region us-west1
```

mike: cheers. if we want lower tail for non-streaming, we should add prefix caching and reduce ideal batch sizes for interactive endpoints.

eva: agreed. will start doc PR. :memo:
